label: Count I — Original / FAC / SAC
title: Breach of Express Contract
legal_theory: Cal. Civ. Code §1620 — express contract requires terms 'stated in words'.
summary: Plaintiffs say a binding written contract emerges from the 2015–2019 founding emails (Exs. 2, 13, 14, 17, 21). The court disagreed: emails alone, however suggestive, are not an express contract.
plaintiff_evidence: Founding emails; Sept 2017 reaffirmations; Musk's $44.56M wired against the alleged contract terms.
defense_response: No single document containing all material terms; assents like 'Agree on all' do not memorialize obligations to remain a nonprofit.

history.text: Dismissed without leave to amend. 'Unlike an implied contract, an express contract is stated in words. Here, the parties agree that there is no one single document that consists of a contract.' (Dkt #163 p.2)

label: Count II — FAC / SAC
title: Breach of Implied-in-Fact Contract
legal_theory: Cal. Civ. Code §1621 — contract inferred from conduct.
summary: Conduct-based contract inferred from the founding meetings, the chain of email assurances, Musk's pattern of donations against those assurances, and the Sept 2017 reaffirmations.
plaintiff_evidence: $44.56M wired over four years; the Sept 2017 reaffirmations preceded ~$10.275M in continued contributions.
defense_response: Plaintiffs cannot identify which terms were agreed; conduct is consistent with charitable solicitation, not contracting.

history.text: Survived the FAC motion to dismiss. The court found Musk adequately pled an implied-in-fact contract.

On Day 5 the court ruled that the operative pre-trial framing collapses Counts II and IV into a restitution-under-quasi-contract theory; there is no standalone unjust-enrichment cause of action under California Supreme Court precedent.

label: Count III — FAC / SAC
title: Breach of Implied Covenant of Good Faith & Fair Dealing
legal_theory: California implied covenant; bad-faith conduct frustrating the contract's purpose.
summary: Plaintiffs alleged defendants 'systematically and unilaterally reinterpreted key terms' and 'obscured OpenAI's for-profit activities'. The court held this was duplicative of the implied-contract claim.

history.text: Dismissed with leave to amend; impermissibly duplicative.

Dismissed without leave on the SAC. Court: 'The Court fails to see how systematically and unilaterally reinterpret[ing] key terms or obscure[ing] OpenAI's for-profit activities alleges any new behavior not encompassed by the preceding list in a nonconclusory manner.'

label: Count IV — FAC / SAC
title: Unjust Enrichment / Quasi-Contract / Restitution
legal_theory: California restitution: 'receipt of a benefit and unjust retention of the benefit at the expense of another.'
parties: Musk v. Altman, Brockman, OpenAI; dismissed as to Microsoft
summary: Even absent a contract, plaintiffs say Altman, Brockman, and OpenAI received and retained Musk's contributions on a charitable premise that has been falsified by the for-profit conversion. The court will instruct the jury that there is no standalone 'unjust enrichment' COA — only restitution under quasi-contract — but the theory continues to trial against the OpenAI defendants.
plaintiff_evidence: $38-$44M traceable into the for-profit's compute, talent, and product, against repeated assurances of nonprofit purpose. Plaintiffs' remedies filings seek disgorgement redirected to the OpenAI charity rather than a personal Musk award.
defense_response: MSJ and pretrial response: Musk made indirect, unrestricted charitable donations through DAFs/YC.org, expected no personal compensation, and cannot disclaim personal injury while asking for a remedy based on personal contributions.
relief: Restitution or disgorgement; recipient and scope disputed in the remedies phase.

history.text: Survived MTD as to OpenAI defendants. Court ordered Musk to elect quasi-contract or unjust enrichment within 30 days of fact-discovery close.
Survived summary judgment against the OpenAI defendants; dismissed against Microsoft.
Musk files a verified waiver disclaiming any award to himself, xAI, or a fund he controls; defendants argue that waiver exposes a no-personal-injury/no-remedy problem.
Court rejects defendants' attempt to rebadge as quantum meruit and refuses plaintiffs' attempt to redirect any restitution to a charity rather than to Musk personally.

label: Count V — FAC / SAC
title: Tortious Interference with Contract
legal_theory: California tort: knowing third-party interference with a valid contract.
summary: Microsoft was alleged to have knowingly induced OpenAI's breach of its contract with Musk via exclusive licensing, exclusive cloud supply, and the Nov 2023 board pressure. The claim did not survive summary judgment.
plaintiff_evidence: Microsoft's $13.75B cumulative investment; Templeton/Hoffman board roles; the Nov 2023 board episode.
defense_response: Microsoft never received conventional equity; the partnership was arm's-length; Microsoft's involvement post-dates the alleged 2015-2017 contract.

history.text: Survived against Microsoft (dismissed against the for-profit entities under California's agent-immunity rule).
Microsoft's MSJ granted as to tortious interference; not part of the April liability trial.

label: Count VI — FAC / SAC
title: Constructive Fraud
legal_theory: Fiduciary or confidential relationship + breach + reliance + damages, no scienter required.
summary: This fraud-adjacent fiduciary-duty theory survived MSJ but was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on the eve of trial after Musk elected to proceed on charitable trust and restitution.

history.text: 'The Court finds Musk has adequately pled the existence of a fiduciary relationship based on a contract or charitable trust.' (Dkt #163 p.5)
Survived OpenAI's MSJ.
Dismissed with prejudice by order after Musk's notice regarding fraud claims.

label: Count VII — FAC / SAC
title: Fraud (Intentional Misrepresentation)
legal_theory: California common-law fraud — false representation, knowledge of falsity, intent to induce reliance, justifiable reliance, damages.
summary: Centered on the September 2017 reaffirmations as false when made. The claim survived MSJ but was dismissed with prejudice before trial so plaintiffs could focus on charitable trust and restitution.
plaintiff_evidence: Altman: 'i remain enthusiastic about the non-profit structure!' (Sept 21, 2017); Zilis report: 'Great with keeping non-profit and continuing to support it' (Sept 22, 2017). Musk continued ~$10.275M of contributions after the reaffirmation.
defense_response: Statements were expressions of present feeling; record is devoid of actionable misrepresentation; Musk had ceased significant funding by Aug 2017; statute of limitations expired in 2022.

history.text: Survived. 'The statements identified as inducing such commitment are actionable non-puffery that meet Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 9(b)'s heightened pleading standards.' Limitations defense rejected on the record.
Survived OpenAI's MSJ.
Dismissed with prejudice by order after Musk's notice regarding fraud claims.

label: Count VIII — FAC
title: Aiding and Abetting Fraud
legal_theory: Cal. tort — knowing assistance to a tortfeasor.
parties: Musk v. For-Profit Entities and Microsoft
summary: Dismissed against everyone. Microsoft's involvement began July 2019 — too late to support liability for 2015–2017 fraudulent promises. For-profit entities barred by California's agent-immunity rule.

history.text: Dismissed. 'Microsoft's involvement in any activity that could plausibly be interpreted as assisting the transition to a for-profit entity did not begin until July 2019…'

label: Count XV — FAC
title: Clayton Act §8 — Interlocking Directorates
legal_theory: 15 U.S.C. §19(a)(1) — per se prohibition on simultaneous service on competitor boards.
parties: xAI v. Microsoft, OpenAI, Hoffman, Templeton
summary: Dismissed for lack of standing. By the time the FAC was filed, Hoffman had resigned (Mar 2023) and Templeton had stepped down (Jul 9, 2024) — four months earlier. Voluntary-cessation doctrine inapplicable when the alleged interlock ended pre-suit.

history.text: Dismissed. 'By the time plaintiffs filed the FAC, four months had passed since the most recent alleged interlock had ended.' (Dkt #121 p.11)

label: Counts VIII–IX — FAC (antitrust)
title: Sherman Act §1 / §2; Cartwright Act; Unfair Practices Act; Clayton Act §3, §7, §14
legal_theory: Federal and California antitrust theories: group boycott, monopolization, exclusive dealing, anticompetitive merger, below-cost pricing.
summary: Centerpiece of plaintiffs' boycott theory: that Microsoft and OpenAI conditioned investment on no-compete with xAI; that exclusive licensing and below-cost compute pricing harmed xAI. The court rejected this at the PI stage as unsupported by admissible evidence.
plaintiff_evidence: FT article October 2024 reporting alleged investor calls; Hoffman/Templeton interlocking-directorate role.
defense_response: Newspaper articles are hearsay; restricting confidential information sharing to non-competing investors is industry-standard pro-competitive practice; xAI raised over $11B.

history.text: Antitrust counts denied at PI; standing fatal in any event. 'xAI admitted that it could not provide a single declaration from an investor to confirm its theory.' (Dkt #121 p.8)

label: Count XVII — FAC
title: False Advertising — Lanham Act
legal_theory: 15 U.S.C. §1125(a)(1)(B) — commercial false statement causing competitor injury.
summary: Dismissed as to Musk for lack of standing (he is not a competitor); xAI's piece may continue but is not on the trial set per the trial-wiki framing.

history.text: Dismissed as to Musk; Musk co-authored the December 2015 statements he claimed reliance on.

label: Count XVIII — FAC / SAC
title: Breach of Charitable Trust
legal_theory: Common-law charitable trust, Cal. Corp. Code §5142(a), and disputed Cal. B&P §17510.8 solicitation theory; settlor or special-interest standing under Restatement (Third) of Trusts §94.
summary: The marquee surviving theory at trial. Plaintiffs allege Musk's contributions created a trust, the corpus of which was the IP, talent, and infrastructure of OpenAI; the for-profit conversion is breach. Defense argues no standing because contributions were routed through DAFs/YC.org and were general-purpose.
plaintiff_evidence: Founding emails; OpenAI's certificate of incorporation; proposed findings at #503; and the §17510.8 theory based on Altman's 2016 funding ask and the July 2020 rent email.
defense_response: OpenAI proposed findings: indirect unrestricted donations, zero donor-restricted assets, no written grant agreement, no breach, limitations. Defendants also argue §17510.6's membership exclusion defeats the §17510.8 path.

history.text: PI denied — likelihood of success a 'toss-up' but irreparable harm and balance of equities were not enough.
MTD denied. The fiduciary-relationship pleading was adequate.
Survived summary judgment against the OpenAI defendants.
Empaneled; one of three live liability theories after the fraud claims were dismissed.
Parties brief the statutory charitable-solicitation route: Musk invokes §17510.8; OpenAI invokes §17510.6's membership exclusion.

label: Count XIX — FAC / SAC
title: Aiding and Abetting Breach of Fiduciary Duty
legal_theory: Cal. tort; substantial assistance + actual knowledge of underlying breach.
summary: Microsoft's remaining exposure is derivative of the charitable-trust theory: plaintiffs must show Microsoft knew about the trust duties and substantially assisted the breach. Microsoft says the founders' dispute predates it, no one told it about Musk-specific donation conditions, and its partnership advanced OpenAI's mission.

history.text: Survived against Microsoft. 'Plaintiffs have plausibly alleged that Microsoft knew of the charitable trust and took steps constituting substantial assistance or encouragement.' (Dkt #163 p.8)
Microsoft's MSJ denied as to aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty.
Microsoft proposed findings frame the claim around no knowledge, no substantial assistance, limitations, laches, and unclean hands.

OpenAI 30(b)(6) witness Robert Wu's deposition was played to the jury. The testimony put trial evidence on Microsoft's target redemptions, the 2023 JDCA license to all IP and technology except AGI, and the non-binding Watershed MOU's post-AGI product-IP terms, without itself resolving knowledge or substantial assistance.

citations.snippet: The target redemption amount for Microsoft's $10,000,000,000 investment is $60,000,000,000.
licensed them all IP and technology... excluding only AGI

label: Counts XXII–XXIV — FAC
title: Derivative claims (breach of fiduciary duty; self-dealing)
legal_theory: Cal. Corp. Code §5233, §5710 — derivative actions on behalf of nonprofit.
parties: Musk, Zilis (derivatively) v. Altman, Brockman; aiding parties
summary: Standing failed because Musk and Zilis were not 'currently' members of OpenAI when the FAC was filed.

history.text: Standing dismissed at PI; confirmed in the MTD ruling.

label: Counts XX–XXI — FAC / SAC
title: Civil RICO §1962(a), (b), (c), (d)
parties: Musk, xAI v. Altman, Brockman, Microsoft, for-profit entities
legal_theory: Pattern of racketeering activity (alleged wire fraud) used to conduct the affairs of an enterprise (OpenAI, Inc.).
summary: FAC pleaded a RICO theory keyed to interstate-wire donation solicitations. The court found §1962(a) and (b) failed for failure to plead alter-ego of Musk and xAI; §1962(c) failed for vague predicate-act pleading.

history.text: (a) and (b) dismissed without leave; (c) dismissed with leave to amend.
(c) re-dismissed without leave on the SAC. 'This reformulation does not add detail on how defendants operated the enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity.' (Dkt #228 p.12)

label: Counterclaim 1 (OpenAI)
title: Cal. UCL §17200 — unfair / fraudulent business practices
legal_theory: Bus. & Prof. Code §17200 (unfair and fraudulent prongs).
summary: OpenAI's narrative: years-long harassment campaign (calls for moratorium, pretextual records demands, X disparagement, the February 2025 'sham' $97.4B LOI) designed to disrupt OpenAI's restructuring and impair its competitive position.

history.text: Survived plaintiffs' MTD. The LOI was protected under California litigation privilege as a settlement-functional communication, but its WSJ publication and media campaign were not.

label: Counterclaim 2 (OpenAI)
title: Tortious interference with prospective economic advantage
legal_theory: California tort: interference with reasonably probable economic relationships.
summary: Anchored in the Feb 2025 LOI media campaign: 'designed to disrupt Counterclaim Plaintiffs' relationships with current and prospective investors and has rendered the performance of those business relationships more costly and burdensome.'

history.text: Survived. Phase II trial.

label: §17510.6 / §17510.8 charitable solicitation
title: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17510.6 / §17510.8
legal_theory: Statutory fiduciary duty arising from the act of soliciting charitable contributions.
summary: Plaintiffs invoke §17510.8 for fiduciary duty on solicitation; defense invokes §17510.6's membership-corporation exception. Court has signaled the §17510.6 exception likely controls under Cohen v. Kabbalah Centre.

history.text: On Day 5 the court signaled §17510.6 trumps §17510.8 under Cohen v. Kabbalah Centre.
